question: A healthy adult takes 1,000 mg of vitamin C a day instead of 200 mg. How much higher does the level in their blood go?
answer: Barely higher at all. Levine's team found blood plasma nearly saturated at about 200 mg a day; at higher doses less was absorbed and the kidneys passed the surplus. At 1,000 mg, most of the extra ended up in urine. A bucket already full does not get any fuller.
move: Past the point of need, more input mostly becomes more waste.
ask: Where am I adding more of something when I already have enough of it?
trap: Five times the dose should give five times the vitamin.
reference: Levine M, Conry-Cantilena C, Wang Y et al., Vitamin C pharmacokinetics in healthy volunteers: evidence for a recommended dietary allowance, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 1996
